translation_notes: The project namespace is `SPDX_NAMESPACE`, not `SPDX`/`spdx`: `from m import spdx:` would not find it. The renaming form of the import does: `from spdx_context import SPDX_NAMESPACE: as spdx:` (the prefix name before `as` is the Python name the module exports, `as` gives the prefix used in the file). Worth knowing for the stratum: project namespaces are often named `X_NAMESPACE`/`X_NS`.

The two `graph.add` on the same subject become ONE `+{ ... a spdx:ExternalDocumentRef ; spdx:spdxDocument ... }`, the third a `+{ }` of its own; `@graph graph` on the parameter. `URIRef(f'{doc_namespace}#{id}')` -> `f<{doc_namespace}#{id}>` and `URIRef(document_uri)` -> `f<{document_uri}>`: equal here since no @base is in scope (a relative document URI stays relative, checked). `RDF` is no longer imported: `a` replaces RDF.type.

Executability: spdx-tools is not installed (and needs eight dependencies); spdx_context.py reproduces the four things the module imports (SPDX_NAMESPACE, Checksum/ChecksumAlgorithm/ExternalDocumentRef as plain dataclasses, add_checksum_to_graph verbatim from spdx/tools-python@cef432adee), and original.py/translated.ldpy import them from there instead of from spdx_tools.*.

Driver: the function returns None, the oracle is the mutation of the graph argument (isomorphism, so the checksum blank node is handled): empty graph + SHA1; BLAKE2B_256 into a graph already holding neighbours; relative URI, odd ref id, SHA3_512. Mutant killed: predicate altered.
optimization_notes: Python: there is nothing to compress (care 1.0). The only change is that the `doc_node` add moves before `add_checksum_to_graph`. The graph is a set, so the order does not matter, and this lets the two sides stay line for line.

Exception to the symmetry rule: ldpy merges the three adds, on two subjects, into ONE `+{ }` (`;` for the shared subject, `.` for the second subject). Only an island lets two subjects share one statement. With a single island, the `(graph)` call suffix is shorter than an `@graph graph` declaration.
`URIRef(f"...")` and `URIRef(document_uri)` become `f<...>`, because no `@base` is in scope. The imports (part of this module region) stay as in original.py and translated.ldpy.
